nodes.name: Electrochemical C-H oxidation of α-pinene
nodes.procedure: α-pinene was subjected to electrochemical C-H oxidation using a 24-well plate electrosynthesis reactor with graphite or RVC anode and nickel cathode. The reaction was carried out at 3.5 V potential at room temperature for 12 hours in a 4 mL reaction volume with stirring at 600 rpm. The electrocatalyst (NHPI, TCNHPI, Quinuclidine, DABCO, or TEMPO) was used at varying equivalences (0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, or 1). The substrate concentration was varied (25, 50, 75, 100, or 125 mM). The electrolyte (LiClO4, LiOTf, Bu4NCIO4, Et4NBF4, or Bu4NPF6) was dissolved in solvent (ACN or ACN/HFIP 19:1 mixture). The reaction yield was determined by NMR spectroscopy monitoring the appearance of signature peaks indicative of ketone or alcohol products.

nodes.description: Electrochemical C-H oxidation of α-pinene to verbenone using random sampling approach

performance_note.value: stagnated at low yields even after extensive iteration

nodes.source_text: Our findings indicate that the random method stagnated at low yields (around 20%) even after extensive iteration, underscoring the inefficiency of nonguided experimental approaches.

nodes.description: Electrochemical C-H oxidation of α-pinene using LLM-driven prediction approach

optimization_approach.value: educated guesses using domain knowledge, usually change one factor at a time

nodes.source_text: While there is excitement and interest in using only LLMs for synthesis optimization, it is important to understand that their 'suggestions' are not based on statistical learning and lack a mathematical foundation. Instead, they reasoned based on observed general trends, made educated guesses using domain knowledge, and tended to usually change one factor at a time.

nodes.description: Electrochemical C-H oxidation of α-pinene using ML-based optimization with Bayesian optimization

optimization_strategy.value: purely statistical approach using expected improvement on Gaussian process

nodes.source_text: ML-based optimization, which applies a purely statistical approach and uses Bayesian optimization (BO) for parameter selection, with code generated by LLMs that utilize expected improvement on a Gaussian process

nodes.description: Electrochemical C-H oxidation of α-pinene using hybrid LLM-ML approach with active learning

optimization_method.value: hybrid LLM-ML approach with active learning

optimization_success.value: rapidly refined reaction conditions through ML algorithms

nodes.source_text: This synergy also enabled the precise tuning of conditions to achieve yields over 60% (Figure 3A and Section S6 of the Supporting Information). Building on the success with α-pinene, we applied the LLM-ML framework to optimize the synthesis conditions for 7 additional substrates (Table S13) with a batch size of four for 10 iterations to demonstrate its generalizability.

nodes.description: Electrochemical C-H oxidation optimization with NHPI electrocatalyst using hybrid LLM-ML active learning approach

optimization_success.value: identified best combination of electrocatalyst, electrolyte, and concentration

nodes.source_text: In total, we successfully identified the best combination of electrocatalyst, electrolyte, and concentration for reaction (Figure 3B) from 1,250 possible combinations within 10 iterations for each of the 8 molecules. Each reaction batch size was 4, with a total of 88 reactions per substrate, including 44 from random sampling and 44 from the integrated method, over 10 iterations plus initialization.

nodes.characterization_summary: Active learning approach combining LLM-guided parameter selection with Bayesian optimization achieved yields over 60% for α-pinene electrochemical C-H oxidation within 10 iterative rounds.
nodes.evidence_snippet: This synergy also enabled the precise tuning of conditions to achieve yields over 60%.
